subject.title: Durable core PR2/6: add optional shared-state foundation

question: Should OpenClaw core own a new shared durable-runtime ledger and top-level durable configuration, or should cross-owner recovery facts remain within the existing task, flow, subagent, delivery, session, and restart owners?
rationale: The submitted implementation creates a persistent core contract and configuration namespace before any active product behavior exists, so code review cannot determine the intended permanent ownership boundary.

options.title: Defer implementation until RFC sponsorship
options.body: Keep the architecture RFC open and close or pause this implementation slice until an owner confirms the residual shared-core boundary.

options.title: Sponsor a narrower core foundation
options.body: Approve only the minimal owner-approved schema and API required by a named current integration, removing inactive configuration and speculative state.

options.title: Keep ownership-specific storage
options.body: Reject the shared ledger and ask for any demonstrated recovery gap to be implemented through the established owning subsystem.

recommendation.title: Defer implementation until RFC sponsorship
recommendation.body: Keep the architecture RFC open and close or pause this implementation slice until an owner confirms the residual shared-core boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor has documented the proposed boundary and can clarify the intended scope, while an upstream product owner must make the final sponsorship decision.
